/.title: Coder | Learn to architect better software
/.description: Learn how to architect the projects you build. Coder helps developers understand project structure, module boundaries and software design through theory and practice.

/theories.title: Senior developer knowledge base: 120 lessons
/theories.description: 120 engineering lessons in 12 modules, in English and Ukrainian: programming principles, architecture, design patterns, algorithms, distributed systems, databases, APIs, security, testing, DevOps, engineering decisions and AI-driven engineering.

/theories/solid-principles.title: SOLID Principles
/theories/solid-principles.description: SOLID groups five object-oriented design heuristics: single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, and dependency inversion.

/theories/dry-don-t-repeat-yourself.title: DRY — Don't Repeat Yourself
/theories/dry-don-t-repeat-yourself.description: DRY means every piece of knowledge should have one authoritative representation.

/theories/kiss-keep-it-simple.title: KISS — Keep It Simple
/theories/kiss-keep-it-simple.description: KISS favors the simplest design that satisfies known requirements and foreseeable risks.

/theories/yagni-you-aren-t-gonna-need-it.title: YAGNI — You Aren't Gonna Need It
/theories/yagni-you-aren-t-gonna-need-it.description: YAGNI discourages building features or abstractions for hypothetical future requirements.

/theories/separation-of-concerns-soc.title: Separation of Concerns (SoC)
/theories/separation-of-concerns-soc.description: Separation of Concerns decomposes a system into parts with distinct responsibilities, such as UI, application workflows, domain rules, and persistence.

/theories/law-of-demeter-lod.title: Law of Demeter (LoD)
/theories/law-of-demeter-lod.description: The Law of Demeter limits an object's knowledge of distant collaborators. 'Talk to your immediate friends' is a heuristic for reducing fragile chains of navigation through internals.

/theories/principle-of-least-astonishmen.title: Principle of Least Astonishment (POLA)
/theories/principle-of-least-astonishmen.description: POLA says an interface should behave in ways its users reasonably expect.

/theories/composition-over-inheritance.title: Composition over Inheritance
/theories/composition-over-inheritance.description: Composition builds behavior by combining focused collaborators, rather than relying on deep inheritance trees.

/theories/high-cohesion-low-coupling.title: High Cohesion, Low Coupling
/theories/high-cohesion-low-coupling.description: Cohesion measures how closely a module's responsibilities belong together; coupling reflects how much it knows about other modules.

/theories/design-by-contract.title: Design by Contract
/theories/design-by-contract.description: Design by Contract specifies preconditions, postconditions, and invariants for components.

/theories/clean-architecture.title: Clean Architecture
/theories/clean-architecture.description: Clean Architecture organizes code around business policies that do not depend on frameworks, databases, or UI details.

/theories/hexagonal-architecture-ports-a.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)
/theories/hexagonal-architecture-ports-a.description: Hexagonal Architecture isolates the application core behind explicit ports.

/theories/onion-architecture.title: Onion Architecture
/theories/onion-architecture.description: Onion Architecture places the domain model at the center and surrounding application, infrastructure, and delivery concerns in concentric layers.

/theories/layered-architecture.title: Layered Architecture
/theories/layered-architecture.description: Layered Architecture divides an application into presentation, business/application logic, and data access responsibilities.

/theories/microservices-architecture.title: Microservices Architecture
/theories/microservices-architecture.description: Microservices split a system into independently deployable services around bounded business capabilities.

/theories/modular-monolith.title: Modular Monolith
/theories/modular-monolith.description: A modular monolith deploys as one application but enforces domain module boundaries internally.

/theories/event-driven-architecture.title: Event-Driven Architecture
/theories/event-driven-architecture.description: Event-Driven Architecture communicates facts about state changes through events.

/theories/cqrs-command-query-responsibil.title: CQRS — Command Query Responsibility Segregation
/theories/cqrs-command-query-responsibil.description: CQRS separates write-side commands that enforce business rules from read-side queries optimized for retrieving information.

/theories/event-sourcing.title: Event Sourcing
/theories/event-sourcing.description: Event Sourcing stores a sequence of domain events as the authoritative record and derives current state by replaying them.

/theories/domain-driven-design-ddd.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD)
/theories/domain-driven-design-ddd.description: Domain-Driven Design aligns software structure with business meaning through shared language, bounded contexts, entities, value objects, aggregates, and domain models.

/theories/gang-of-four-gof-design-patter.title: Gang of Four (GoF) Design Patterns
/theories/gang-of-four-gof-design-patter.description: The 23 GoF patterns describe recurring object collaboration and creation solutions.

/theories/grasp-responsibility-assignmen.title: GRASP — Responsibility Assignment
/theories/grasp-responsibility-assignmen.description: GRASP is a set of principles for deciding which object or component should own behavior.

/theories/dependency-injection.title: Dependency Injection
/theories/dependency-injection.description: Dependency Injection supplies collaborators from outside a component instead of constructing them internally.

/theories/repository-pattern.title: Repository Pattern
/theories/repository-pattern.description: A Repository presents a collection-like interface for domain objects and hides persistence operations.

/theories/unit-of-work.title: Unit of Work
/theories/unit-of-work.description: Unit of Work tracks and coordinates changes that must be persisted together, usually under one transaction.

/theories/factory-method-and-abstract-fa.title: Factory Method & Abstract Factory
/theories/factory-method-and-abstract-fa.description: Factory Method delegates creation of a product to subclasses or specialized creators; Abstract Factory creates related families of products through a common contract.

/theories/strategy-and-observer-patterns.title: Strategy & Observer Patterns
/theories/strategy-and-observer-patterns.description: Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface.

/theories/adapter-and-facade-patterns.title: Adapter & Facade Patterns
/theories/adapter-and-facade-patterns.description: Adapter translates one interface into another expected by a client.

/theories/state-and-command-patterns.title: State & Command Patterns
/theories/state-and-command-patterns.description: State delegates behavior according to an object's current lifecycle state; Command packages an action as an object or message.

/theories/mvc-mvp-and-mvvm.title: MVC, MVP & MVVM
/theories/mvc-mvp-and-mvvm.description: MVC, MVP and MVVM are presentation architecture patterns that separate visual behavior from domain logic in different ways.

/theories/big-o-notation.title: Big O Notation
/theories/big-o-notation.description: Big O describes an asymptotic upper bound on how resource use grows with input size, often used for time or memory complexity.

/theories/time-and-space-complexity.title: Time & Space Complexity
/theories/time-and-space-complexity.description: Time complexity estimates work as input scales; space complexity estimates additional memory or total storage required.

/theories/arrays-lists-stacks-and-queues.title: Arrays, Lists, Stacks & Queues
/theories/arrays-lists-stacks-and-queues.description: These linear data structures trade indexing, insertion, removal and ordering guarantees.

/theories/hash-tables-and-trees.title: Hash Tables & Trees
/theories/hash-tables-and-trees.description: Hash tables optimize key-based lookup under suitable hashing assumptions; trees represent hierarchy or maintain ordered search.

/theories/graphs-and-graph-algorithms.title: Graphs & Graph Algorithms
/theories/graphs-and-graph-algorithms.description: Graphs model entities and relations as vertices and edges.

/theories/sorting-and-searching.title: Sorting & Searching
/theories/sorting-and-searching.description: Sorting establishes order so data can be presented or searched efficiently.

/theories/recursion-and-dynamic-programm.title: Recursion & Dynamic Programming
/theories/recursion-and-dynamic-programm.description: Recursion solves a problem by invoking the same operation on smaller instances.

/theories/greedy-algorithms.title: Greedy Algorithms
/theories/greedy-algorithms.description: A greedy algorithm repeatedly makes a locally favorable choice without reconsidering earlier decisions.

/theories/caching-algorithms.title: Caching Algorithms
/theories/caching-algorithms.description: Caching trades storage and invalidation complexity for reduced recomputation or I/O.

/theories/concurrency-algorithms.title: Concurrency Algorithms
/theories/concurrency-algorithms.description: Concurrency techniques coordinate operations that can overlap in time.

/theories/cap-theorem.title: CAP Theorem
/theories/cap-theorem.description: CAP states that, when a network partition occurs, a distributed data system cannot guarantee both linearizable consistency and availability for every request.

/theories/pacelc-theorem.title: PACELC Theorem
/theories/pacelc-theorem.description: PACELC extends CAP: if partitioned, choose between availability and consistency; else, even in normal operation, choose between latency and consistency.

/theories/acid-transactions.title: ACID Transactions
/theories/acid-transactions.description: ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability of database transactions.

/theories/base-model.title: BASE Model
/theories/base-model.description: BASE describes a family of distributed-system trade-offs often summarized as Basically Available, Soft state and Eventual consistency.

/theories/eventual-consistency.title: Eventual Consistency
/theories/eventual-consistency.description: Eventual consistency means replicas converge to a compatible state if updates stop and communication proceeds, under the system's stated assumptions.

/theories/idempotency.title: Idempotency
/theories/idempotency.description: An operation is idempotent when applying it more than once has the same intended effect as applying it once.

/theories/consensus-algorithms.title: Consensus Algorithms
/theories/consensus-algorithms.description: Consensus allows distributed participants to agree on a sequence of decisions despite certain failures.

/theories/distributed-transactions-and-s.title: Distributed Transactions & Sagas
/theories/distributed-transactions-and-s.description: Distributed business workflows often span independent services that cannot share one ACID transaction.

/theories/circuit-breaker-pattern.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
/theories/circuit-breaker-pattern.description: A circuit breaker prevents repeated calls to an unhealthy dependency from exhausting resources and cascading failures.

/theories/retry-timeout-and-backoff-patt.title: Retry, Timeout & Backoff Patterns
/theories/retry-timeout-and-backoff-patt.description: Timeouts bound waiting, retries recover transient failures, and backoff spaces repeated attempts to avoid overload.

/theories/database-normalization-1nf-5nf.title: Database Normalization (1NF–5NF)
/theories/database-normalization-1nf-5nf.description: Normalization organizes relational tables to reduce unintended redundancy and modification anomalies.

/theories/denormalization.title: Denormalization
/theories/denormalization.description: Denormalization deliberately duplicates or precomputes data to improve read performance, simplify queries or support specific access patterns.

/theories/indexing-strategies.title: Indexing Strategies
/theories/indexing-strategies.description: Indexes accelerate targeted reads by maintaining auxiliary structures, often at the cost of extra storage and slower writes.

/theories/query-optimization.title: Query Optimization
/theories/query-optimization.description: Query optimization reduces database resource use and latency while preserving semantics.

/theories/transaction-isolation-levels.title: Transaction Isolation Levels
/theories/transaction-isolation-levels.description: Transaction isolation defines which effects of concurrent transactions can become visible and which anomalies are permitted.

/theories/optimistic-vs-pessimistic-lock.title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking
/theories/optimistic-vs-pessimistic-lock.description: Optimistic concurrency checks whether data changed before committing; pessimistic locking reserves exclusive access earlier.

/theories/sharding-and-partitioning.title: Sharding & Partitioning
/theories/sharding-and-partitioning.description: Partitioning splits a dataset into manageable segments; sharding distributes segments across nodes.

/theories/replication-strategies.title: Replication Strategies
/theories/replication-strategies.description: Replication maintains multiple copies of data for availability, read scale or geographic proximity.

/theories/sql-vs-nosql-trade-offs.title: SQL vs NoSQL Trade-offs
/theories/sql-vs-nosql-trade-offs.description: SQL and NoSQL describe broad families of data models and interfaces, not simple 'consistent versus scalable' opposites.

/theories/schema-evolution-and-migration.title: Schema Evolution & Migrations
/theories/schema-evolution-and-migration.description: Schema evolution changes stored structure while preserving existing data and service compatibility.

/theories/rest-principles.title: REST Principles
/theories/rest-principles.description: REST is an architectural style for networked systems emphasizing resources, uniform interfaces, stateless interactions, layered components and representations.

/theories/graphql-architecture.title: GraphQL Architecture
/theories/graphql-architecture.description: GraphQL lets clients request typed fields through a schema and supports queries, mutations and subscriptions.

/theories/rpc-and-grpc.title: RPC & gRPC
/theories/rpc-and-grpc.description: Remote Procedure Call presents network operations as service methods; gRPC commonly uses Protocol Buffers, HTTP/2 and generated contracts.

/theories/api-versioning.title: API Versioning
/theories/api-versioning.description: API versioning manages incompatible contract changes without unexpectedly breaking clients.

/theories/authentication-vs-authorizatio.title: Authentication vs Authorization
/theories/authentication-vs-authorizatio.description: Authentication establishes who or what is making a request; authorization determines what that principal may do.

/theories/oauth-2-0-and-openid-connect.title: OAuth 2.0 & OpenID Connect
/theories/oauth-2-0-and-openid-connect.description: OAuth 2.0 is a framework for delegated authorization; OpenID Connect builds an authentication identity layer on top.

/theories/rate-limiting-and-throttling.title: Rate Limiting & Throttling
/theories/rate-limiting-and-throttling.description: Rate limiting constrains request frequency or cost; throttling delays or rejects traffic to protect capacity and fairness.

/theories/pagination-and-filtering.title: Pagination & Filtering
/theories/pagination-and-filtering.description: Pagination bounds response size and enables scalable navigation; filtering selects records according to an explicit query contract.

/theories/webhooks-and-message-queues.title: Webhooks & Message Queues
/theories/webhooks-and-message-queues.description: Webhooks deliver events via outbound HTTP calls; message queues broker asynchronous delivery between producers and consumers.

/theories/backward-compatibility.title: Backward Compatibility
/theories/backward-compatibility.description: Backward compatibility lets newer systems continue serving existing clients and stored data.

/theories/cia-triad.title: CIA Triad
/theories/cia-triad.description: The CIA triad identifies three fundamental security properties: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.

/theories/principle-of-least-privilege.title: Principle of Least Privilege
/theories/principle-of-least-privilege.description: Least privilege gives identities and processes only the permissions necessary for their assigned tasks, ideally for the shortest required period.

/theories/zero-trust-architecture.title: Zero Trust Architecture
/theories/zero-trust-architecture.description: Zero Trust treats network location as insufficient proof of trust and requires explicit identity, device/workload context and policy for access decisions.

/theories/defense-in-depth.title: Defense in Depth
/theories/defense-in-depth.description: Defense in Depth uses multiple independent security controls so a single error or compromise does not expose the entire system.

/theories/owasp-top-10.title: OWASP Top 10
/theories/owasp-top-10.description: The OWASP Top 10 is an awareness list of major web-application risk categories, not a full security checklist.

/theories/threat-modeling-stride.title: Threat Modeling (STRIDE)
/theories/threat-modeling-stride.description: STRIDE is a threat-identification framework: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service and Elevation of privilege.

/theories/secure-software-development-li.title: Secure Software Development Lifecycle
/theories/secure-software-development-li.description: A Secure SDLC integrates security decisions and verification throughout planning, design, implementation, delivery and operations.

/theories/cryptography-fundamentals.title: Cryptography Fundamentals
/theories/cryptography-fundamentals.description: Cryptography protects information and proves authenticity using well-studied primitives: symmetric encryption, public-key cryptography, cryptographic hashes, MACs and digital signatures.

/theories/secrets-management.title: Secrets Management
/theories/secrets-management.description: Secrets management controls creation, distribution, use, rotation and revocation of credentials such as API keys, database passwords and signing keys.

/theories/software-supply-chain-security.title: Software Supply Chain Security
/theories/software-supply-chain-security.description: Supply chain security protects dependencies, build systems, artifacts and publishing workflows from malicious or compromised components.

/theories/testing-pyramid.title: Testing Pyramid
/theories/testing-pyramid.description: The testing pyramid recommends many fast, focused tests and fewer expensive full-system tests.

/theories/test-driven-development-tdd.title: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
/theories/test-driven-development-tdd.description: TDD follows a short red-green-refactor loop: write a failing test, implement the minimal behavior, then improve design without changing behavior.

/theories/behavior-driven-development-bd.title: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
/theories/behavior-driven-development-bd.description: BDD connects business examples to executable specifications through collaboration among developers, testers and domain stakeholders.

/theories/unit-integration-and-end-to-en.title: Unit, Integration & End-to-End Testing
/theories/unit-integration-and-end-to-en.description: These testing levels differ in boundary and realism: unit tests isolate a small behavior; integration tests exercise interacting components; E2E tests validate a full user or system journey.

/theories/property-based-testing.title: Property-Based Testing
/theories/property-based-testing.description: Property-based testing checks general invariants over many generated inputs rather than only hand-picked examples.

/theories/contract-testing.title: Contract Testing
/theories/contract-testing.description: Contract testing verifies assumptions between service providers and consumers, such as request shapes, response semantics and event schemas.

/theories/mutation-testing.title: Mutation Testing
/theories/mutation-testing.description: Mutation testing changes code in small controlled ways and checks whether the test suite detects those changes.

/theories/static-analysis.title: Static Analysis
/theories/static-analysis.description: Static analysis inspects source or compiled representations without executing full application behavior.

/theories/code-smells-and-refactoring.title: Code Smells & Refactoring
/theories/code-smells-and-refactoring.description: Code smells are symptoms of possible design problems, not automatic proof that code is wrong.

/theories/technical-debt-management.title: Technical Debt Management
/theories/technical-debt-management.description: Technical debt describes future engineering cost caused by design and implementation shortcuts or changing needs.

/theories/ci-cd-principles.title: CI/CD Principles
/theories/ci-cd-principles.description: Continuous Integration merges and validates changes frequently; Continuous Delivery keeps releases deployable; Continuous Deployment automatically releases changes passing defined gates.

/theories/infrastructure-as-code-iac.title: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
/theories/infrastructure-as-code-iac.description: IaC defines infrastructure resources in version-controlled declarations or programs.

/theories/immutable-infrastructure.title: Immutable Infrastructure
/theories/immutable-infrastructure.description: Immutable infrastructure replaces running instances with newly built images rather than patching them in place.

/theories/blue-green-and-canary-deployme.title: Blue-Green & Canary Deployment
/theories/blue-green-and-canary-deployme.description: Blue-green deployment switches traffic between two complete environments; canary deployment gradually exposes a subset of traffic to a new version.

/theories/observability-logs-metrics-and.title: Observability: Logs, Metrics & Traces
/theories/observability-logs-metrics-and.description: Observability allows engineers to infer a system's internal state from emitted evidence.

/theories/sli-slo-and-sla.title: SLI, SLO & SLA
/theories/sli-slo-and-sla.description: An SLI is a quantitative service reliability indicator; an SLO is a target for that indicator; an SLA is a contractual commitment, often with consequences.

/theories/fault-tolerance.title: Fault Tolerance
/theories/fault-tolerance.description: Fault tolerance lets a system continue delivering acceptable behavior when components fail.

/theories/scalability-vs-elasticity.title: Scalability vs Elasticity
/theories/scalability-vs-elasticity.description: Scalability is the ability to handle more load by adding resources or optimizing design.

/theories/load-balancing.title: Load Balancing
/theories/load-balancing.description: Load balancing distributes requests or work across instances to improve utilization, capacity and availability.

/theories/disaster-recovery-rpo-and-rto.title: Disaster Recovery: RPO & RTO
/theories/disaster-recovery-rpo-and-rto.description: Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data-loss window; Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is the target time to restore service after a disruption.

/theories/system-design-trade-offs.title: System Design Trade-offs
/theories/system-design-trade-offs.description: System design is the deliberate choice among imperfect alternatives under explicit requirements.

/theories/cost-benefit-analysis.title: Cost–Benefit Analysis
/theories/cost-benefit-analysis.description: Cost–benefit analysis estimates whether expected business value justifies implementation, maintenance and risk.

/theories/build-vs-buy.title: Build vs Buy
/theories/build-vs-buy.description: Build-versus-buy asks whether a capability should be developed in-house, purchased as software or outsourced.

/theories/conway-s-law.title: Conway's Law
/theories/conway-s-law.description: Conway's Law observes that system designs tend to reflect the communication structures of the organizations creating them.

/theories/brooks-s-law.title: Brooks's Law
/theories/brooks-s-law.description: Brooks's Law warns that adding people to a late software project may make it later because onboarding and communication cost time.

/theories/amdahl-s-law.title: Amdahl's Law
/theories/amdahl-s-law.description: Amdahl's Law bounds the speedup of a workload when only part can be parallelized.

/theories/little-s-law.title: Little's Law
/theories/little-s-law.description: Little's Law relates long-run average number of items in a stable system, arrival/completion rate and average time in system: L equals lambda multiplied by W.

/theories/pareto-principle.title: Pareto Principle
/theories/pareto-principle.description: The Pareto principle is a heuristic that a minority of causes often account for a majority of outcomes.

/theories/theory-of-constraints.title: Theory of Constraints
/theories/theory-of-constraints.description: The Theory of Constraints holds that overall throughput is limited by a small number of bottlenecks.

/theories/architecture-decision-records-.title: Architecture Decision Records (ADR)
/theories/architecture-decision-records-.description: An ADR records an architectural choice, the context that motivated it, alternatives, consequences and status.

/theories/specification-driven-developme.title: Specification-Driven Development
/theories/specification-driven-developme.description: Specification-driven development starts with an explicit, testable description of required behavior before implementation.

/theories/context-engineering.title: Context Engineering
/theories/context-engineering.description: Context engineering curates the information, tools and constraints available to an AI model for a task.

/theories/prompt-engineering.title: Prompt Engineering
/theories/prompt-engineering.description: Prompt engineering structures instructions and examples to make model output more relevant, constrained and verifiable.

/theories/agentic-workflows.title: Agentic Workflows
/theories/agentic-workflows.description: Agentic workflows let AI systems plan, call tools, modify artifacts and iterate toward a goal.

/theories/human-in-the-loop-hitl.title: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
/theories/human-in-the-loop-hitl.description: Human-in-the-loop design requires a person to review or approve important AI decisions and actions.

/theories/ai-code-review.title: AI Code Review
/theories/ai-code-review.description: AI-generated code needs the same or stronger review as human-written code.

/theories/ai-assisted-testing.title: AI-Assisted Testing
/theories/ai-assisted-testing.description: AI can accelerate test-case discovery, fixture creation and failure analysis, but generated tests still need an independent behavioral oracle.

/theories/model-evaluation-and-benchmark.title: Model Evaluation & Benchmarking
/theories/model-evaluation-and-benchmark.description: Model evaluation measures whether an AI system performs particular tasks reliably under relevant constraints.

/theories/ai-security-and-prompt-injecti.title: AI Security & Prompt Injection
/theories/ai-security-and-prompt-injecti.description: Prompt injection occurs when untrusted content tries to redirect an AI system's instructions or tool use.

/theories/ai-generated-code-governance.title: AI-Generated Code Governance
/theories/ai-generated-code-governance.description: AI-generated code governance establishes policies for provenance, accountability, quality, security and licensing across AI-assisted delivery.

/practices.title: Practice: 120 exercise sets for developers
/practices.description: 1,800 exercises and 60 system design challenges in English and Ukrainian: for every lesson 10 checked questions and 5 written tasks, and for 12 architecture templates build, fix, extend, optimize and review challenges.

/practices/challenge/sys-01-build.title: Community event reservations: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-01-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. A town events site needs public listings, signed-in reservations, organizer cancellations and email confirmations.

/practices/challenge/sys-01-fix.title: Repair unsafe browser shortcuts: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-01-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. An AI agent connected the frontend directly to the database and email provider; the API lost its identity check.

/practices/challenge/sys-01-extend.title: Safe document uploads: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-01-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Organizers must upload PDF schedules and event posters.

/practices/challenge/sys-01-optimize.title: Ticket sale traffic spike: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-01-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. A release attracts 8,000 visits/minute.

/practices/challenge/sys-01-review.title: Choose the first deployment model: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-01-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. A three-person team must launch in eight weeks with uncertain demand and 2,000 projected daily users.

/practices/challenge/sys-02-build.title: Training academy modules: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-02-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. A small academy needs courses, enrollment, billing and instructor schedules.

/practices/challenge/sys-02-fix.title: Restore business module ownership: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-02-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. Orders no longer consults Catalog.

/practices/challenge/sys-02-extend.title: Promotions and partial refunds: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-02-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. The commerce monolith gains discounts and partial refunds.

/practices/challenge/sys-02-optimize.title: Reporting slows checkout: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-02-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. During month-end reporting, checkout p95 grows from 200 ms to 1.8 s due to heavy joins and long-lived transactions.

/practices/challenge/sys-02-review.title: Extract Billing or keep it?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-02-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. One eight-person team ships monthly.

/practices/challenge/sys-03-build.title: Food delivery service boundaries: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-03-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Customers order restaurant meals, authorize payment and await courier pickup.

/practices/challenge/sys-03-fix.title: Repair payment ownership: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-03-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. Orders gained direct access to the payment database and PSP, while Payments stopped consuming the broker.

/practices/challenge/sys-03-extend.title: Loyalty points on completed orders: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-03-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. A new Loyalty service awards points after completed paid orders and reverses them on refunds.

/practices/challenge/sys-03-optimize.title: Inventory reservation latency: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-03-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. Order confirmation reaches p99 4.5 s; some consumers lag 30 s.

/practices/challenge/sys-03-review.title: Independent services or distributed monolith?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-03-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. Catalog, Orders and Inventory deploy separately but share schemas and demand coordinated releases by one team.

/practices/challenge/sys-04-build.title: Multi-tenant team tracker: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-04-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Organizations create workspaces, invite members and pay per seat.

/practices/challenge/sys-04-fix.title: Cross-tenant data leak: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-04-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. The API bypasses tenant and role checks and admin UI accesses the shared database directly.

/practices/challenge/sys-04-extend.title: Metered usage-based billing: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-04-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Customers pay for active seats plus exported reports and API requests.

/practices/challenge/sys-04-optimize.title: Noisy tenant overwhelms workers: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-04-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. One tenant runs exports that starve others of DB connections.

/practices/challenge/sys-04-review.title: Shared database versus tenant isolation: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-04-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. A hundred small customers share infrastructure; two regulated enterprises request separate backups and data residency.

/practices/challenge/sys-05-build.title: Small electronics shop: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-05-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. A shop sells limited-stock devices, accepts online payments and ships parcels.

/practices/challenge/sys-05-fix.title: Payment bypasses stock: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-05-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. Cart directly invokes the PSP, the browser reads orders storage and the stock reservation step disappeared.

/practices/challenge/sys-05-extend.title: Returns and partial refunds: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-05-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Shoppers may return order lines within 14 days; warehouse inspection can approve part of a return and reject damaged items.

/practices/challenge/sys-05-optimize.title: Flash sale inventory contention: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-05-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. 200 units are on sale, but 20,000 shoppers try checkout within one minute.

/practices/challenge/sys-05-review.title: Synchronous or asynchronous checkout?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-05-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. API response target is 800 ms; PSP calls sometimes take 3 s and warehouse holds another 2 s.

/practices/challenge/sys-06-build.title: Service-company CRM: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-06-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. A repair company tracks clients, visits, quotations, employees and invoices.

/practices/challenge/sys-06-fix.title: Permissions and audit removed: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-06-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. A refactor removed API permission checks and Sales audit, adding a UI-to-transaction-database shortcut.

/practices/challenge/sys-06-extend.title: Purchase approval workflow: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-06-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Staff submit expense requests.

/practices/challenge/sys-06-optimize.title: Two-million-record reporting: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-06-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. A dashboard takes 18 s due to joins on transactional tables with two million activities.

/practices/challenge/sys-06-review.title: One ERP or independent departments?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-06-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. HR, Sales and Finance want separate release cycles, yet their data is interdependent and one platform team operates everything.

/practices/challenge/sys-07-build.title: Local services booking marketplace: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-07-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Clients reserve tutors, cleaners and technicians.

/practices/challenge/sys-07-fix.title: Stop seller self-payout: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-07-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. A seller UI can invoke settlement directly, and buyers can publish reviews without a valid purchase.

/practices/challenge/sys-07-extend.title: Disputes and partial refunds: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-07-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. A client disputes a finished service.

/practices/challenge/sys-07-optimize.title: Search index lag: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-07-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. New listings appear in search after ten minutes; deleted ones linger because the indexing queue stalls.

/practices/challenge/sys-07-review.title: Build settlement or buy a provider?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-07-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. The startup wants split payouts and platform fees.

/practices/challenge/sys-08-build.title: Collaborative whiteboard: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-08-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Up to 50 editors share a board, see cursors and reconnect after a network outage.

/practices/challenge/sys-08-fix.title: Unauthorized message storage: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-08-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. A socket layer now writes to storage without message service checks; a browser can also write directly.

/practices/challenge/sys-08-extend.title: Offline edits with conflicts: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-08-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Editors can stay offline for 20 minutes and return with conflicting operations.

/practices/challenge/sys-08-optimize.title: Ten thousand live viewers: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-08-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. A room has 10,000 watchers and 20 editors.

/practices/challenge/sys-08-review.title: WebSocket, SSE or polling?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-08-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. A monitoring dashboard updates every 5–10 seconds, with very few user commands.

/practices/challenge/sys-09-build.title: Offline field inspections: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-09-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Inspectors fill forms and upload photographs at remote sites with unreliable connectivity.

/practices/challenge/sys-09-fix.title: Mobile security bypass: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-09-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. An agent removed secure credential storage and API auth, then connected mobile and push systems directly to the server database.

/practices/challenge/sys-09-extend.title: Resumable photos and conflicts: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-09-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. Two workers may edit the same inspection.

/practices/challenge/sys-09-optimize.title: Battery-hungry background sync: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-09-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. The app polls every 10 seconds even with no changes.

/practices/challenge/sys-09-review.title: Local-first or online-first booking?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-09-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. A mobile scheduling app must work through brief outages, but scarce appointment slots cannot be booked twice.

/practices/challenge/sys-10-build.title: Durable order event pipeline: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-10-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. An accepted order must persist and trigger billing, inventory and reports.

/practices/challenge/sys-10-extend.title: Version OrderCreated events: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-10-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. OrderCreated v1 contains customerId and total.

/practices/challenge/sys-10-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. A broker has 1,000,000 queued events.

/practices/challenge/sys-10-review.title: Event sourcing or state plus events?: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-10-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. Billing requires a strong audit trail and corrections.

/practices/challenge/sys-11-build.title: Internal company knowledge assistant: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-11-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Staff ask private policy questions.

/practices/challenge/sys-11-fix.title: Prompt-injection tool bypass: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-11-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. Policy checks were bypassed; retrieved text is connected to tool execution and the orchestrator can call external services directly.

/practices/challenge/sys-11-extend.title: AI architecture code reviewer: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-11-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. AI reviews pull requests against the 120 theories.

/practices/challenge/sys-11-optimize.title: RAG cost and latency reduction: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-11-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. Knowledge replies average 14 s at $0.12 each.

/practices/challenge/sys-11-review.title: AI agent autonomy policy: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-11-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. An assistant can draft emails, create support tickets and propose refunds under $50.

/practices/challenge/sys-12-build.title: Cold-chain temperature telemetry: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-12-build.description: Build challenge, intermediate, 45 min. Sensors on trucks report temperatures every minute; operators receive alerts and can change safe set-points.

/practices/challenge/sys-12-fix.title: Unsafe direct device commands: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-12-fix.description: Fix challenge, intermediate, 30 min. The MQTT broker stopped verifying registry identity, and a dashboard can actuate devices directly.

/practices/challenge/sys-12-extend.title: Staged over-the-air firmware updates: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-12-extend.description: Extend challenge, intermediate, 40 min. A fleet of 3,000 devices needs signed updates; failures must halt rollout, and offline devices can update days later.

/practices/challenge/sys-12-optimize.title: Reconnect telemetry storm: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-12-optimize.description: Optimize challenge, advanced, 45 min. 100,000 devices reconnect, producing 100,000 readings/minute.

/practices/challenge/sys-12-review.title: Cloud authority versus edge autonomy: system design challenge
/practices/challenge/sys-12-review.description: Review challenge, advanced, 30 min. Building access controllers must preserve safe emergency exits during WAN outages.

/practices/dry-don-t-repeat-yourself.title: DRY — Don't Repeat Yourself: exercises
/practices/dry-don-t-repeat-yourself.description: 15 exercises on DRY — Don't Repeat Yourself: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. DRY means every piece of knowledge should have one authoritative representation.

/practices/yagni-you-aren-t-gonna-need-i.title: YAGNI — You Aren't Gonna Need It: exercises
/practices/yagni-you-aren-t-gonna-need-i.description: 15 exercises on YAGNI — You Aren't Gonna Need It: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. YAGNI discourages building features or abstractions for hypothetical future requirements.

/practices/separation-of-concerns-soc.title: Separation of Concerns (SoC): exercises

/practices/law-of-demeter-lod.title: Law of Demeter (LoD): exercises

The Law of Demeter limits an object's knowledge of distant collaborators. 'Talk to your immediate friends' is a heuristic for reducing fragile chains of navigation through internals.

/practices/principle-of-least-astonishme.title: Principle of Least Astonishment (POLA): exercises
/practices/principle-of-least-astonishme.description: 15 exercises on Principle of Least Astonishment (POLA): 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. POLA says an interface should behave in ways its users reasonably expect.

/practices/composition-over-inheritance.title: Composition over Inheritance: exercises
/practices/composition-over-inheritance.description: 15 exercises on Composition over Inheritance: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Composition builds behavior by combining focused collaborators, rather than relying on deep inheritance trees.

/practices/high-cohesion-low-coupling.title: High Cohesion, Low Coupling: exercises
/practices/high-cohesion-low-coupling.description: 15 exercises on High Cohesion, Low Coupling: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Cohesion measures how closely a module's responsibilities belong together; coupling reflects how much it knows about other modules.

/practices/design-by-contract.title: Design by Contract: exercises
/practices/design-by-contract.description: 15 exercises on Design by Contract: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Design by Contract specifies preconditions, postconditions, and invariants for components.

/practices/clean-architecture.description: 15 exercises on Clean Architecture: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Clean Architecture organizes code around business policies that do not depend on frameworks, databases, or UI details.

/practices/hexagonal-architecture-ports-.title: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters): exercises
/practices/hexagonal-architecture-ports-.description: 15 exercises on Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters): 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Hexagonal Architecture isolates the application core behind explicit ports.

/practices/onion-architecture.title: Onion Architecture: exercises
/practices/onion-architecture.description: 15 exercises on Onion Architecture: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Onion Architecture places the domain model at the center and surrounding application, infrastructure, and delivery concerns in concentric layers.

/practices/layered-architecture.title: Layered Architecture: exercises
/practices/layered-architecture.description: 15 exercises on Layered Architecture: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Layered Architecture divides an application into presentation, business/application logic, and data access responsibilities.

/practices/microservices-architecture.title: Microservices Architecture: exercises
/practices/microservices-architecture.description: 15 exercises on Microservices Architecture: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Microservices split a system into independently deployable services around bounded business capabilities.

/practices/modular-monolith.title: Modular Monolith: exercises

/practices/event-driven-architecture.title: Event-Driven Architecture: exercises
/practices/event-driven-architecture.description: 15 exercises on Event-Driven Architecture: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Event-Driven Architecture communicates facts about state changes through events.

/practices/cqrs-command-query-responsibi.description: 15 exercises on CQRS — Command Query Responsibility Segregation: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. /practices/domain-driven-design-ddd.title: Domain-Driven Design (DDD): exercises
/practices/domain-driven-design-ddd.description: 15 exercises on Domain-Driven Design (DDD): 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Domain-Driven Design aligns software structure with business meaning through shared language, bounded contexts, entities, value objects, aggregates, and domain models.

/practices/gang-of-four-gof-design-patte.title: Gang of Four (GoF) Design Patterns: exercises
/practices/gang-of-four-gof-design-patte.description: 15 exercises on Gang of Four (GoF) Design Patterns: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. The 23 GoF patterns describe recurring object collaboration and creation solutions.

/practices/grasp-responsibility-assignme.title: GRASP — Responsibility Assignment: exercises
/practices/grasp-responsibility-assignme.description: 15 exercises on GRASP — Responsibility Assignment: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. GRASP is a set of principles for deciding which object or component should own behavior.

/practices/dependency-injection.title: Dependency Injection: exercises
/practices/dependency-injection.description: 15 exercises on Dependency Injection: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Dependency Injection supplies collaborators from outside a component instead of constructing them internally.

/practices/repository-pattern.title: Repository Pattern: exercises
/practices/repository-pattern.description: 15 exercises on Repository Pattern: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. A Repository presents a collection-like interface for domain objects and hides persistence operations.

/practices/unit-of-work.title: Unit of Work: exercises
/practices/unit-of-work.description: 15 exercises on Unit of Work: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Unit of Work tracks and coordinates changes that must be persisted together, usually under one transaction.

/practices/factory-method-and-abstract-f.title: Factory Method & Abstract Factory: exercises
/practices/factory-method-and-abstract-f.description: 15 exercises on Factory Method & Abstract Factory: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Factory Method delegates creation of a product to subclasses or specialized creators; Abstract Factory creates related families of products through a common contract.

/practices/strategy-and-observer-pattern.title: Strategy & Observer Patterns: exercises
/practices/strategy-and-observer-pattern.description: 15 exercises on Strategy & Observer Patterns: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Strategy encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind a common interface.

/practices/adapter-and-facade-patterns.title: Adapter & Facade Patterns: exercises
/practices/adapter-and-facade-patterns.description: 15 exercises on Adapter & Facade Patterns: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Adapter translates one interface into another expected by a client.

/practices/state-and-command-patterns.title: State & Command Patterns: exercises
/practices/state-and-command-patterns.description: 15 exercises on State & Command Patterns: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. State delegates behavior according to an object's current lifecycle state; Command packages an action as an object or message.

/practices/mvc-mvp-and-mvvm.description: 15 exercises on MVC, MVP & MVVM: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. MVC, MVP and MVVM are presentation architecture patterns that separate visual behavior from domain logic in different ways.

/practices/big-o-notation.description: 15 exercises on Big O Notation: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Big O describes an asymptotic upper bound on how resource use grows with input size, often used for time or memory complexity.

/practices/arrays-lists-stacks-and-queue.description: 15 exercises on Arrays, Lists, Stacks & Queues: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. These linear data structures trade indexing, insertion, removal and ordering guarantees.

/practices/hash-tables-and-trees.title: Hash Tables & Trees: exercises
/practices/hash-tables-and-trees.description: 15 exercises on Hash Tables & Trees: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Hash tables optimize key-based lookup under suitable hashing assumptions; trees represent hierarchy or maintain ordered search.

/practices/graphs-and-graph-algorithms.title: Graphs & Graph Algorithms: exercises
/practices/graphs-and-graph-algorithms.description: 15 exercises on Graphs & Graph Algorithms: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Graphs model entities and relations as vertices and edges.

/practices/sorting-and-searching.title: Sorting & Searching: exercises

/practices/recursion-and-dynamic-program.description: 15 exercises on Recursion & Dynamic Programming: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Recursion solves a problem by invoking the same operation on smaller instances.

/practices/greedy-algorithms.title: Greedy Algorithms: exercises
/practices/greedy-algorithms.description: 15 exercises on Greedy Algorithms: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. A greedy algorithm repeatedly makes a locally favorable choice without reconsidering earlier decisions.

/practices/caching-algorithms.title: Caching Algorithms: exercises
/practices/caching-algorithms.description: 15 exercises on Caching Algorithms: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Caching trades storage and invalidation complexity for reduced recomputation or I/O.

/practices/concurrency-algorithms.description: 15 exercises on Concurrency Algorithms: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Concurrency techniques coordinate operations that can overlap in time.

/practices/cap-theorem.title: CAP Theorem: exercises
/practices/cap-theorem.description: 15 exercises on CAP Theorem: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. CAP states that, when a network partition occurs, a distributed data system cannot guarantee both linearizable consistency and availability for every request.

/practices/pacelc-theorem.title: PACELC Theorem: exercises
/practices/pacelc-theorem.description: 15 exercises on PACELC Theorem: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. PACELC extends CAP: if partitioned, choose between availability and consistency; else, even in normal operation, choose between latency and consistency.

/practices/acid-transactions.title: ACID Transactions: exercises
/practices/acid-transactions.description: 15 exercises on ACID Transactions: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability of database transactions.

/practices/indexing-strategies.title: Indexing Strategies: exercises

/practices/query-optimization.title: Query Optimization: exercises
/practices/query-optimization.description: 15 exercises on Query Optimization: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Query optimization reduces database resource use and latency while preserving semantics.

/practices/transaction-isolation-levels.title: Transaction Isolation Levels: exercises
/practices/transaction-isolation-levels.description: 15 exercises on Transaction Isolation Levels: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Transaction isolation defines which effects of concurrent transactions can become visible and which anomalies are permitted.

/practices/optimistic-vs-pessimistic-loc.title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking: exercises

/practices/sharding-and-partitioning.title: Sharding & Partitioning: exercises

/practices/replication-strategies.title: Replication Strategies: exercises
/practices/replication-strategies.description: 15 exercises on Replication Strategies: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Replication maintains multiple copies of data for availability, read scale or geographic proximity.

/practices/sql-vs-nosql-trade-offs.description: 15 exercises on SQL vs NoSQL Trade-offs: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. SQL and NoSQL describe broad families of data models and interfaces, not simple 'consistent versus scalable' opposites.

/practices/schema-evolution-and-migratio.title: Schema Evolution & Migrations: exercises
/practices/schema-evolution-and-migratio.description: 15 exercises on Schema Evolution & Migrations: 10 questions that are checked for you and 5 written tasks. Schema evolution changes stored structure while preserving existing data and service compatibility.
